html:
A Buddhist temple at Ikaruga, near Nara in Japan, founded around 607 by Prince Shōtoku and Empress Suiko. Its main hall and five-storey pagoda are among the oldest wooden buildings in the world.

The Nihon Shoki says the first temple burned in 670. It was rebuilt soon after, and the western precinct was standing by around 711. Tree-ring dating shows the central pillar of the pagoda came from a tree cut in the late 500s.

The temple keeps the look of early Chinese and Korean Buddhist building, much of which has vanished on the mainland. Inside are some of the oldest Buddhist statues in Japan, made in the generations after Buddhism reached Japan. In 1993 it was among the first sites in Japan named to the UNESCO World Heritage list, together with Himeji Castle.
